text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

Government bank Banco do Brasil, France's Coface and local insurance firms Bradesco, Bamerindus, Sul America and Minas Brasil are signing today a protocol for the creation of an insurance company for exports.
-- BRAZIL WILL BUY MORE ARGENTINE CARS
Brazil will purchase 85,000 more cars from Argentina within a period of three years. In 1997, Brazilian automakers will have to buy 28,000 vehicles.
-- ITALY LINKS PC FARIAS TO DRUG TRAFFICKING
Italy's Police and Justice found evidence that Paulo Cesar Farias, ex-treasurer of former President Fernando Collor, was involved with a drug trafficking network managed by the Italian Mafia.
-- VOTORANTIM IN TALKS WITH INVESTORS TO BUY CVRD

Brazil's Grupo Votorantim is holding talks with Japan's Nippon Steel to form a consortium to acquire control of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce. The group is likely to include Banco Safra, Vale's employees and pension funds.
-- LANDS OF FAILED BANKS WILL BE USED FOR AGRARIAN REFORM
Farms belonging to failed banks Economico, Nacional, Banorte and Mercantil will be acquired by the Agrarian Reform Ministry to settle 7,000 landless families.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
